items.title: CVE-2026-104766 - Appointment Booking Plugin <= 5.7.3 - Authenticated (Custom+) Privilege Escalation to 'settings[default_wp_role_for_customer]' Parameter
items.one_liner: A privilege escalation vulnerability in the LatePoint WordPress plugin lets users with specific custom roles elevate new customer accounts to administrators.
items.summary: An authenticated privilege escalation vulnerability has been identified in the Appointment Booking Plugin (LatePoint) for WordPress in all versions up to and including 5.7.3. The flaw stems from the `OsSettingsController::update()` handler iterating over unvalidated user-supplied settings and `OsSettingsHelper::prepare_value()` lacking proper role validation for the `default_wp_role_for_customer` setting. Authenticated users holding a custom role with the `settings__edit` capability can exploit this to change the default registration role to administrator. Consequently, any newly registered customer through LatePoint gains full WordPress administrator privileges.
items.bottom_line: LatePoint booking plugin up to version 5.7.3 contains a privilege escalation flaw allowing authenticated agents to grant administrator privileges to new customer accounts.

claims.support_span: This makes it possible for authenticated attackers holding a LatePoint role with the settings__edit capability (such as an agent or custom role) to overwrite the default WordPress role for new customers with administrator, causing any subsequently self-registered LatePoint customer account to be created with full WordPress administrator privileges.

items.one_liner: A new CLI plugin enables easy access to OpenAI's multimodal Decisions API for structured classification tasks.
items.summary: OpenAI has released the Decisions API, a new tool for classification tasks that supports text and image inputs. A new plugin, `llm-openai-decisions`, has been developed to integrate this API with the LLM CLI tool, allowing users to run predicate, choice, or score queries.
